references.text: John the Baptist speaks of baptizing with the Holy Spirit and fire, which prepares for Jesus' command to baptize in the name of the Holy Trinity.
Jesus commands the disciples to preach the gospel and baptize those who believe, which resembles the command in Matthew 28:19.

Peter tells the people to repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ to receive forgiveness of sins and the gift of the Holy Spirit, reflecting the significance of baptism mentioned in Matthew 28:19.

The apostles in Jerusalem send Peter and John to Samaria, where they pray for the new believers so that they may receive the Holy Spirit, showing the early church's practice of baptism and receiving the Holy Spirit.
When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus, demonstrating obedience to Jesus' command regarding baptism.
God says He will pour out His Spirit on all flesh, which can be seen as a precursor to the baptism in the Holy Spirit that Jesus commands in Matthew 28:19.
